summary: Over the 14-day evaluation period, glycemic outcomes are exceptional with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, standard deviation of 15.1 mg/dL, coefficient of variation of 12.9%, and 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL).

Profile basal rates maintain overnight glucose near target (102-107 mg/dL). SMB and UAM automation safely absorb postprandial excursions, including transient peaks up to 188 mg/dL during high-carb weekend brunches, returning glucose to baseline within 4 hours without late hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: 1,345 valid CGM entries over 14 days provide 100% data coverage with 0 gaps greater than 15 minutes. Complete treatment records include 28 carbohydrate treatments (1,448g total) and 28 meal boluses (142.2U total).
analysis_steps.evidence: CGM entry count = 1,345/1,345 expected; 0 gaps > 15 min; 28 treatments logged in Nightscout telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Glucose control is extremely stable with zero significant hypoglycemia burden and negligible hyperglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR (70-180 mg/dL) = 99.7%, TAR (>180 mg/dL) = 0.3%, TBR (<70 mg/dL) = 0.0%, average glucose = 117.0 mg/dL, CV = 12.9%. Minor nadirs of 70-71 mg/dL occurred around 03:00 UTC on Aug 11 and Aug 17.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates (0.85 U/h) successfully maintain flat baseline glucose within target range (95-110 mg/dL). Daytime glucose elevations are postprandial rather than baseline basal drift.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local average glucose from 00:00 to 06:00 ranges between 102.3 mg/dL and 107.5 mg/dL. Scheduled targets are 95-110 mg/dL (00:00), 90-105 mg/dL (06:00), and 100-115 mg/dL (22:00).

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios (10-12 g/U) and ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U) are well-calibrated. Postprandial excursions peak at 120 minutes during weekend brunches (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise) but consistently resolve to baseline within DIA (5.5 h).
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch (68g carbs / 5.8U bolus) peaks at 188 mg/dL at 120 min, returning to 111-115 mg/dL by 240 min. Weekday breakfast (42g carbs / 4.2U) peaks at 157-167 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are active and deliver appropriate micro-bolus corrections without causing insulin stacking or secondary hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3, max_smb_basal_minutes=45, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30. Postprandial glucose recovers smoothly across all 28 logged meal windows.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety caps (max_basal = 2.4 U/h, max_iob = 8.0 U) provide adequate headroom for loop operation while protecting against excessive automated insulin delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal (2.4 U/h) is ~2.3x max scheduled basal (1.05 U/h). Max IOB (8.0 U) is ~1.4x typical largest meal bolus (5.8 U). Carbohydrate absorption max is set to 6.0 hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific boolean flags for autosens_enabled and dynamic_sensitivity_enabled are null in exported raw settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal bolus strategies (20-min prebolus for breakfast, 10-min for brunch) align well with observed glycemic control. Brunch shows transient peak touch of 188 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Breakfast (42g carbs, 20-min prebolus, 70% immediate) results in mild 120-min rise (+33 to +57 mg/dL). Brunch (68g carbs, 10-min prebolus, 60% immediate) results in higher 120-min rise (+62 to +70 mg/dL).

analysis_steps.findings: Declared extended carbs (20g over 120 min for weekend brunch) successfully prevent late-tail hyperglycemia without requiring manual split boluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch therapy response windows show steady recovery from 188 mg/dL at 120 min to 115 mg/dL at 240 min and 111 mg/dL at 360 min.

analysis_steps.findings: No changes are recommended for core profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets). The system functions with exceptionally high efficiency. Minor prebolus timing optimization for weekend brunch can be tested independently.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, CV 12.9%, mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL across 14 full days.

strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range across 14 continuous days.
Highly stable overnight glucose maintenance around 102-107 mg/dL on scheduled basal rate of 0.85 U/h.
Very low glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9% and Standard Deviation of 15.1 mg/dL.
Effective integration of SMB and UAM micro-boluses resolving meal excursions within 4 hours without late-window hypoglycemia.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peaks touching 188 mg/dL (+70 mg/dL rise) occur 120 minutes following higher-carbohydrate weekend brunch meals.

recommendations.title: Test Slightly Extended Prebolus for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch meals currently peak at 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes before resolving back to 115 mg/dL by 240 minutes. Increasing prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15 minutes, or increasing immediate bolus percentage from 60% to 70%, may blunt the 2-hour peak while maintaining safe 4-hour recovery.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all profile basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and target settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall glucose metrics demonstrate optimal clinical control (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV). Automated loop delivery effectively manages postprandial peaks without insulin stacking or hypoglycemia.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe 120-minute postprandial peak during the next 2-3 weekend brunch meals to evaluate if prebolus timing optimization flattens the peak below 160 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current prebolus times (20 min for fast-carb breakfast, 10 min for weekend brunch) and immediate bolus split percentages, relying on automated SMB/UAM delivery to resolve postprandial excursions.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Overall glucose outcomes are exceptional (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR). Automated SMB and UAM interventions successfully control postprandial rises without secondary hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether extending the Weekend Brunch prebolus from 10 to 15 minutes reduces the transient 120-minute peak below 160 mg/dL without causing pre-meal hypoglycemia.

exceptions.suggestion: Test increasing prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15 minutes or immediate bolus portion from 60% to 70%.
exceptions.rationale: Higher-carbohydrate brunch (68g) causes a brief 120-minute peak of 188 mg/dL (+70 mg/dL rise) before loop automation returns glucose to 115 mg/dL by 240 minutes.

implementation_steps: Review current profile parameters with your diabetes care team; all basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA settings are performing optimally and should be retained.
Verify in the AAPS user interface that SMB activation conditions and sensitivity settings match your intended daily preferences.
If blunting the transient 2-hour peak during weekend brunch is desired, test extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes for one brunch meal while keeping total insulin unchanged.
Monitor postprandial glucose continuously for 4 hours following any behavioral test to confirm safe recovery without hypoglycemia.
education: Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) above 70% is the standard clinical goal for automated insulin delivery; achieving 99.7% TIR indicates optimal alignment across basal rates, carb ratios, and algorithm settings.
A Coefficient of Variation (CV) below 36% reflects stable glycemic control; a CV of 12.9% demonstrates very low day-to-day glucose fluctuation.

Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS help model slow-absorbing meals (like high-fat brunches) over time, allowing SMB micro-boluses to match late digestion without requiring a manual dual-wave bolus.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only. Consult your healthcare provider before modifying any diabetes management parameters.
Make setting or timing adjustments one at a time, and evaluate outcomes over multiple days before making further changes.
Always maintain fast-acting glucose available for hypoglycemia treatment, even when Time Below Range is 0.0%.
